audit_findings.title: FY2026 anchor appears to retain a one-time legal recovery
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.3 million pretax; approximately $3.85 million after the filed 27.3% tax rate. If the $0.4 million interest component was already purged, the remaining exposure is $4.9 million pretax or $3.56 million after tax, approximately $1.96 per share of BASE value and $1.37 per share of buy-below value if capitalized using the existing model.
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring recovery retained in anchor OE is projected through the explicit forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase was primarily attributable to the recognition of $5.3 million related to proceeds received in connection with a legal matter against Wright Printing Company, its owners Mark Wright, and CEO Mardra Sikora, which includes $0.4 million of interest income.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the recovery is nonrecurring, but the supplied record does not demonstrate whether the OE calculation removed it. If retained, the estimated $1.37 per-share effect on the buy-below level exceeds the $0.32 gap between the $21.78 threshold and the $21.46 market price, so it is reasonably capable of reversing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $5.3 million between other income, taxes and FY2026 OE, confirm treatment of the separately identified $0.4 million interest component, and rerun every scenario after removing any retained after-tax recovery.

audit_findings.title: Growth may require recurring acquisitions whose cost is excluded from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $64.726 million of acquisition cash spending in FY2024-FY2026, including $38.930 million in FY2026; FY2026 organic sales fell $25.0 million while acquired revenue added $22.8 million. The recurring maintenance-acquisition requirement is unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth and terminal assumptions credit acquired earnings, while acquisition spending needed to replace organic attrition is excluded from OE and reinvestment requirements.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, there can be no assurance that suitable acquisition opportunities will be available in the future, which could harm our strategic business plan as acquisitions are part of our strategy to offset normal print attrition.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate both continuing organic attrition and material acquisition spending that substantially replaced lost revenue. They do not establish how much acquisition spending is recurrently required, but omitting a maintenance-acquisition charge while forecasting nonnegative growth can materially overstate distributable cash and terminal value.
audit_findings.action: Separate organic and acquired revenue, margins and OE; estimate the purchase consideration required to replace recurring organic earnings attrition; then rerun OE and all growth cases with that maintenance-acquisition investment charged.

audit_findings.title: The 2.5% perpetual growth assumption conflicts with secular demand erosion
audit_findings.magnitude: Terminal value represents 47.7%-50.9% of operating PV, approximately $300.0 million in BEAR, $369.3 million in BASE and $422.5 million in BULL.
audit_findings.mechanism: The 2.5% terminal growth rate directly increases terminal OE and the terminal capitalization multiple.
audit_findings.evidence: The printing industry continues to experience weakening demand for printed products.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates weakening print demand, organic sales declines and reliance on acquisitions to offset attrition. It does not prove that 2.5% perpetual growth is impossible, but the assumption is unsupported without acquisition reinvestment and affects roughly half of operating value, making it plainly capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Build long-run organic volume, price, margin and reinvestment evidence, then rerun each scenario with zero and negative terminal growth and with any required acquisition spending deducted.

audit_findings.title: The bridge treats all cash and short-term investments as excess
audit_findings.magnitude: $49.082 million, or approximately $1.93 per share and $1.35 per share of buy-below value. Reclassifying approximately $11.64 million as required cash would eliminate the current $0.32 price-to-buy-below cushion.
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for operations, collateral or committed uses should remain with the operating business rather than being added separately in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our principal cash requirements include payments to vendors in the ordinary course of business, capital expenditures, compensation and benefits, and dividends to shareholders.
audit_findings.explanation: The record confirms the full $49.082 million was added and identifies operating cash requirements, but it does not establish the minimum cash balance. Because classifying only about 24% of the balance as non-excess would erase the stated purchase cushion, the unresolved classification is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the May 31 cash balance to restricted or collateralized cash, declared or committed payments, acquisition funding and a supportable minimum operating-cash requirement; rerun the bridge using only unrestricted excess cash.

audit_findings.title: A structurally higher inventory requirement may be missing from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 inventory increased $16.098 million, including a $14.484 million increase in raw materials; the FY2026 cash-flow statement records a $12.848 million inventory use of cash excluding acquisition effects. The recurring sustaining amount is unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: A permanent increase in required working capital reduces OE when funded; excluding or normalizing away that investment would overstate sustainable distributable cash.
audit_findings.evidence: In anticipation of this disruption, we made a strategic decision to increase inventory levels to mitigate the risk of shortages and ensure continuity of supply.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a large inventory build, but the record does not show whether the $52.9 million OE anchor already includes the relevant working-capital outflow or how much inventory will remain necessary after the supplier transition. A one-time build already charged to OE should not be charged perpetually, while an omitted structural requirement could be material; the present record cannot distinguish those cases.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the FY2026 OE calculation to the filed working-capital changes, isolate acquisition-related inventory, determine the stabilized carbonless-paper buffer, and rerun only for any sustaining investment omitted from OE.

audit_findings.title: Pending lease litigation could exceed the recorded reserve
audit_findings.magnitude: More than $4.0 million was originally sought versus approximately $0.5 million accrued, an original pleaded gap exceeding $3.5 million; $3.5 million equals approximately $0.14 per share or $0.10 per share of buy-below value. The exposure remaining after dismissed and abandoned claims is unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: Any probable loss exceeding the recorded reserve is an additional liability deductible in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The landlord sought more than $4.0 million in repair costs and other consequential damages even though the landlord sold the facility without making the supposedly necessary repairs.
audit_findings.explanation: The pending surviving claim creates a possible bridge shortfall, but no excess loss has been demonstrated. The known $3.5 million comparison relates to the original demand and is smaller than the $0.32 purchase cushion after applying the MOS; however, the filing supplies neither an upper bound nor a valuation of the surviving claim, so materiality cannot presently be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the post-trial ruling and latest contingency disclosure, identify the surviving damages and applicable insurance or tax effects, and deduct any probable after-tax exposure above the recorded $0.5 million reserve.
